# core/hkdf.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/hkdf.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

HKDF with HMAC-SHA-256 or HMAC-SHA-384 (RFC 5869), the
key derivation that TLS 1.3 uses.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, `hkdf_extract`
returns 32 bytes (`hkdf_extract384` 48) and `hkdf_expand` returns exactly
the number of bytes asked for (at most 8160 bytes, below the 255 blocks the
RFC allows), with the hash its key is the output of: SHA-256 for 32 bytes,
SHA-384 for 48. Not
proved: that the output is RFC 5869's; the tests check its vectors.

`import "core/hkdf.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha256.bastio](core-sha256.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`hkdf_extract`](#hkdf_extract) | The pseudo-random key of the input key material `ikm` under `salt`. |
| [`hkdf_extract384`](#hkdf_extract384) | The pseudo-random key of the input key material `ikm` under `salt` with HMAC-SHA-384. |
| [`hkdf_expand`](#hkdf_expand) | `n` bytes of output key material from the pseudo-random key `prk` (32 bytes. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `hkdf_extract`

```bastio
fn hkdf_extract(salt: &Bytes, ikm: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 32
```

The pseudo-random key of the input key material `ikm` under `salt`: 32
bytes. An empty salt is the same as 32 zero bytes, as the RFC says.

Example:

```bastio
let salt = bfrom("salt");
let ikm = bfrom("input key material");
let prk = hkdf_extract(salt, ikm);
let n = blen(prk);
bfree(prk);
bfree(ikm);
bfree(salt);
if n != 32 { return 1; }
```

### `hkdf_extract384`

```bastio
fn hkdf_extract384(salt: &Bytes, ikm: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 48
```

The pseudo-random key of the input key material `ikm` under `salt` with
HMAC-SHA-384: 48 bytes. An empty salt is the same as 48 zero bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let salt = bfrom("salt");
let ikm = bfrom("input key material");
let prk = hkdf_extract384(salt, ikm);
let n = blen(prk);
bfree(prk);
bfree(ikm);
bfree(salt);
if n != 48 { return 1; }
```

### `hkdf_expand`

```bastio
fn hkdf_expand(prk: &Bytes, info: &Bytes, n: u64) -> Bytes
  requires n <= 8160 && (blen(prk) == 32 || blen(prk) == 48)
  ensures blen(result) == n
```

`n` bytes of output key material from the pseudo-random key `prk` (32
bytes: HMAC-SHA-256, 48 bytes: HMAC-SHA-384) and the context `info`.

Example:

```bastio
let salt = bfrom("salt");
let ikm = bfrom("input key material");
let info = bfrom("context");
let prk = hkdf_extract(salt, ikm);
let okm = hkdf_expand(prk, info, 42);
let n = blen(okm);
bfree(okm);
bfree(prk);
bfree(info);
bfree(ikm);
bfree(salt);
if n != 42 { return 1; }
```
